content.text:
**Finding: deviation (critical) — Section 21.1 cap quantum.**

Section 21 looks compliant on its face — mutual cap, mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (with data-restoration, replacement-service, notice and incident-response costs preserved as direct damages), a full set of uncapped Excluded Claims, and Customer's payment obligation expressly excluded from the cap. The defect is in the cap basis: it is measured by "Fees", which §§ 1.5–1.6 define as the Implementation Fee only — a one-time USD 12,000 charge under the first Order Form. Combined with the "first Order Form" limitation, the cap collapses to roughly USD 12,000 regardless of actual spend, i.e. an illusory cap well below the 6-months'-fees walk-away line.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) makes the minimum change to reach the preferred position, leaving the mutual and carve-out architecture untouched:

> …shall not exceed the ~~Fees~~ **greater of (a) all amounts** paid or payable by Customer under ~~the first Order Form~~ **this Agreement and all Order Forms** during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim **and (b) USD 1,000,000**.

The "Fees" definition itself was left alone to avoid disturbing the payment provisions.
